title: fix: make availability KPI trends legible
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Shows normalized 5xx errors per 1,000 valid requests as the primary health view
- Keeps precise service and community-model availability percentages
- Preserves raw 5xx counts and corrects lower-is-better trend coloring
- Adds focused KPI coverage for formatting and missing data

Tests: `npm test -- --run test/kpis.test.js`; `npm run build`

gist.headline: The charts learned context
gist.blurb: Availability KPIs now lead with normalized 5xx errors per 1,000 valid requests, because a raw error count without traffic context is just a number having a bad day.
gist.summary: The operations KPI dashboard now presents normalized 5xx errors per 1,000 valid requests as its primary health signal, retains precise service and community-model availability percentages and raw error counts, and correctly colors lower-is-better trends.
gist.impact: Operators can compare service health across changing traffic levels more clearly, with reliable trend colors and safer handling of missing KPI data.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy operations garden where Polli helps a CRT-monitor robot read a health chart: a small, clearly labeled normalized-error gauge sits beside precise availability percentage flowers, while downward trend arrows glow reassuringly. Code-plants and a few tiny missing-data placeholders communicate observability and resilient formatting.
